subject: Customer alert — queue backups and per-tenant evictions causing error surge
messages:
From: Angelo Rossi <angelo.rossi@blueharbor.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High p99 and 5xx spike on prod - traces attached

Laura —

We started seeing a sharp p99 latency increase and a corresponding rise in 5xx on our production traffic around 08:45 PT. This correlates with a huge number of KV evictions on your side (I can see repeated prefix misses in the traces). The errors are throttling our user-facing pipeline. Attached are a few stack traces and a short capture of request headers.

What we see:
- p99 jumped from ~220ms to >1.8s
- 5xx rate went from 0.1% to ~3.2% for our tenant
- Logs show frequent prefix misses and eviction churn (lots of short-lived hot keys)

Can you confirm if there were any config changes or rollout around that time? We are blocked for a morning release if this persists. Please escalate if needed — we need an ETA on mitigation.

Attachments: blueharbor-sample-traces.txt

Thanks,
Angelo
Oncall, BlueHarbor
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Angelo Rossi <angelo.rossi@blueharbor.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 and 5xx spike on prod - traces attached

Angelo —

Thank you for the heads up and for the traces. I'm escalating internally now.
Immediate notes: no control plane rollout targeted at BlueHarbor at 08:45 PT from what my team shows, but we did push a default KV eviction-policy tweak to the staging pool earlier this morning that was meant to be limited. I'm asking Infra to verify if that landed against your dedicated pool.

Action items I am kicking off:
- Rishi: can you confirm if the KV policy change touched any shared defaults or routing for us?
- Monica: I'll take point on customer comms; can you confirm their P0 window and message?
- Markus: tagging for priority — this looks like a cross-team config/serving interaction and will need exec visibility if the mitigation is not quick.

I'll follow up with an internal summary in 15.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 and 5xx spike on prod - traces attached

Laura / team —

I've pulled the traces Angelo sent and our internal metrics. Preliminary diagnosis below (summary first, details after):

Summary:
- Root cause: eviction/churn in the KV prefix cache combined with batch-lane starvation. A small number of very heavy requests are creating long-running generation batches that monopolize batch lanes and delay short requests (HOL blocking). The ongoing churn causes eviction storms for frequently-used prefixes (cache thrash), which amplifies token-generation latency and increases error/window timeouts.
- Likely trigger: an inadvertent change to the default eviction aggressiveness (lowered TTL and smaller per-lane cache quota) that was rolled to non-isolated pools earlier this morning. The change was intended for staging only — investigating why it applied to BlueHarbor's routing group.

Immediate mitigations (implement in this order):
1) Temporarily constrain max_batch_size and per-request token_limit for BlueHarbor to reduce long-tail batch duration (hotfix - rtn in 5m).
2) Increase per-tenant hot-lane weight and reserve a single hot-lane for prefixes with >X QPS to protect short requests.
3) Roll back the eviction aggressiveness change for BlueHarbor's pool (apply kv_policy_patch.yaml attached) as a canary to 10% of their nodes, monitor 15m p99.
4) Throttle/queue large requests at the routing edge (rate limit by token_count) to prevent HOL cascades until a full fix lands.

Longer term (postmortem scope):
- Tighten gating so control-plane changes to eviction defaults require explicit namespace isolation.
- Add an automated hotkey detector that pre-allocates prefix cache and moves prefixes into prefetch mode instead of evicting.
- Improve observability for batch lane wait times and expose lane-level metrics per-tenant in the console.

Attachments: kv_policy_patch.yaml (small policy patch to revert TTL and quota for affected pool), flamegraph-prefetch.png (visualization of lane blocking)

I'm applying the temporary limits now and will POST status in 5 minutes.

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Angelo Rossi <angelo.rossi@blueharbor.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 and 5xx spike on prod - traces attached

Angelo —

Thanks for the quick report. We're implementing mitigations now:
- Applying per-tenant throttle and max_batch caps (effective immediately).
- Rolling the kv policy rollback via canary (10% of nodes) and will widen if p99 improves.

Customer comms:
- BlueHarbor, we are actively throttling large requests to prevent further customer impact and reverting a KV eviction policy that appears to have propagated outside staging. We expect material improvement to p99 within 20–30 minutes after the canary widens. I'll send an update at +30 and +60.

If things do not improve within the hour, we'll prepare an executive brief and a credit request.

— Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary for leadership — BlueHarbor latency incident

Markus —

Quick exec summary for leadership inbox:
- Incident: BlueHarbor experienced p99 latency and 5xx spike due to KV cache thrash and batch-lane HOL blocking triggered by an unintended policy rollout.
- Impact: Customer-facing errors for a high-volume tenant; blocked a morning release for BlueHarbor; estimated exposure window ~2.5 hours before mitigations.
- Containment: Applied throttles and reduced max_batch_size; rolled back eviction aggressiveness as a 10% canary then widened after positive signal; reserving hot-lane allocations for heavy prefixes. P99 back to baseline for canary nodes, widening continues.
- Next steps: postmortem ownership (Rishi), change-control policy update (Infra lead), hotkey prefetch feature as engineering ticket.
- Customer ask: BlueHarbor will want an explanation and potential service credit; Monica is drafting language.

Please advise if you want this escalated to the exec incident channel or if we should continue on the current path.

— Laura
Head of Customer Reliability
